name: Fern & Kettle
description: A made-up two-person online tea shop (loose-leaf tea, a few teapots), used as the example team. Nothing here is a real business.

humans.name: Leo
humans.summary: Partner. Same as Ana: decisions and approvals.

roles.name: Lead
roles.summary: Orchestrator: breaks work down, assigns it, chases what's stuck

roles.name: Dev
roles.summary: The storefront code: pages, checkout, fixes

roles.name: Reviewer
roles.summary: Reviews every pull request once and merges it when it's good

roles.name: Marketing
roles.summary: Product pages, newsletter drafts, what to promote this week

roles.name: Support
roles.summary: Customer questions, order problems, reply drafts

rules: Anything that leaves the shop: emails to customers or suppliers (always through propose_email), posts, ads.
Spending money: a new paid tool, ads, a supplier order.
Prices, discounts and refunds above the support policy in TEAM.md.
Merging a pull request that touches checkout, payments or prices.
Changing production outside a reviewed pull request.

heartbeat.prompt: Heartbeat ({now}). Look at the backlog (open issues and PRs, the team log). Assign the most valuable next steps, one clear task each, and chase anything stuck for more than a day. If nothing is worth doing, post_update "nothing to move" and stop.

routines.name: morning-check
routines.prompt: Morning check ({now}): run the tests on a clean checkout, list PRs open for more than a day. Share one short message only if something is wrong.

routines.name: weekly-promo
routines.prompt: Weekly promo ({now}): pick one product to feature this week and draft the newsletter. Ask for approval with the draft; nothing goes out without it.

triggers.name: new-support-tickets
triggers.prompt:
New customer messages ({name}). Draft a reply for each and send the drafts to the humans in one request_approval:
{items}
